channel.title: CyNews 24 (EN)
channel.description: CyNews 24 brings you the latest Cyprus news today in English, Russian and Greek: politics, economy, real estate, society, tourism and sport, with sources linked.

item.title: Hundreds Dress in White as Limassol Bids Farewell to 17-Year-Old Schoolgirl
item.description: Mourners dressed in white gathered in Limassol on November 24 for the funeral of 17-year-old Kyriaki Anastasiou as authorities await lab test results.

item.title: Cyprus weighs cap on short-term rental beds in overtourism hotspots
item.description: A new carrying-capacity study will map areas at risk of saturation. Where overtourism is confirmed, the state plans to cap tourist beds, starting with short-term rentals.

item.title: 17-year-old Limassol student dies in Kakopetria hotel; minister asks for review of unsupervised trips
item.description: At about 11pm on Saturday a 17-year-old pupil from Limassol was found unconscious in a Kakopetria hotel room. Resuscitation failed. Police are investigating, and a post-mortem is expected on Monday. Education Minister Athena Michaelidou offered condolences and said the ministry does not approve such trips.

item.title: YOO Limassol, Pyrgos: what the project site and Property Gallery publish
item.description: An independent YOO Limassol review. This is not a sale and not a partnership. The project site says 81 villas and 84 apartments. Property Gallery’s sales page says 80 villas and a start of 2,965,000, with no VAT line.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus recall 249 cars in Cyprus over Takata airbags
item.description: On Friday the road transport department warned that a faulty airbag can cause serious injury or death, and advised owners not to drive the cars until the part is replaced. The deadline for the repair is eight months.

item.title: Cyprus drops the extra approval some non-EU workers needed after four years
item.description: Reports on Friday said a ministerial committee removed the special approval that general-employment workers from outside the EU needed to renew a residence and work permit after four years. The jobs named include kitchen staff, carers, waiters, bakeries and cheese-makers.

item.title: A Paphos resident reports €9,304 in cryptocurrency missing after an account-security call
item.description: On Thursday he complained to the Paphos criminal investigation department: a man claiming to work for a payments platform persuaded him to install programs on his computer. Cryptocurrency then disappeared from an online account.

item.title: Fire at a Pallouriotissa beer bar: about 50 people waited on balconies, and a 37-year-old is in serious condition
item.description: At about 2:45 on Saturday a fire started at the entrance of a first-floor venue. Police later said a preliminary inspection pointed to a deliberate blaze set with flammable material.

item.title: Overnight checks: 642 vehicles stopped, 25 drink-drivers reported and five people arrested
item.description: On Friday night, police across the island checked 820 people and 48 premises. Of 415 breath tests, 25 drivers were reported. Five people were arrested, for offences including drugs, unlawful stay and drink-driving.

item.title: ONE Limassol: what Pafilia publishes about the tower on 28th October Avenue
item.description: An independent ONE Limassol review. This is not a Pafilia listing. The developer’s pages say 37 storeys, 83 homes and a start of €1,700,000 plus VAT. In 2021 Pafilia wrote about first handovers. Its 2026 guide still offers what remains.

item.title: Minthis Residences: what Pafilia publishes about the homes at Minthis Hills
item.description: An independent Minthis Residences review. This is not a listing. Pafilia’s page gives homes of 220–333 m² and energy class A. It states no sale price and no home count.

item.title: Limassol Blu Marine: what Leptos publishes about the seafront towers
item.description: An independent Limassol Blu Marine review. This is not a listing. A Poseidon studio on the project page is €658,000 plus VAT. A June 2026 company text said Cavalli “from €845,000”.

item.title: Avakoum monastery trial: a witness put unreceipted collections at €3.62 million
item.description: On Friday the head of the tax-fraud investigation unit told the Nicosia permanent criminal court how the service calculated the Osios Avvakoum monastery’s collections and a tax bill of €285,067.49. The hearing resumes on 30 November.

item.title: Parliament unanimously tightens the rules on taking water in Cyprus
item.description: On Thursday the House amended the Integrated Water Management Law: periodic reviews of permits, a double fee to license old works, and a fine served within 30 days of detection.

item.title: Akel tables a bill to cancel camera fines that are not served within 180 days
item.description: The bill is before the transport committee and has not been passed. The party wants penalty points added on the day of the offence, not the day of payment. The transport ministry, the MP said, is against the idea.

item.title: Environmental groups ask parliament not to make planning exemptions routine
item.description: The federation Opok said economic benefit on its own does not justify a large private development where the rules do not allow it. The statement came as the interior committee opened the subject after an audit warning.

item.title: EAC moves the old net-metering deadline: papers are due by 28 February 2027
item.description: The extension covers only applications for kilowatt-hour netting filed by 31 December 2025. New systems go to net billing. Two reports give different dates for the final connection.

item.title: KEAN, Limassol: what the Cyprus Mail reported about bbf’s factory site
item.description: An independent reading of the Cyprus Mail piece of 18 January 2026 on KEAN. This is not a listing. The article states no sale price and no build timetable.

item.title: Parliament unanimously passes a water law: unlicensed abstraction can be stopped, and a backdated permit costs double
item.description: The Water Development Department will be able to order a halt to abstraction started without a permit. The fine depends on how serious the breach is and how it affects the resource. MPs passed the law and immediately said the island still has no single water authority.

item.title: MPs split on the cable’s price: from 8 cents less per kilowatt-hour to a 10–15% higher bill
item.description: At Thursday’s plenary, Disy, Diko and Elam backed the Great Sea Interconnector, while Akel, Alma and Direct Democracy demanded figures. The forecasts MPs offered for the electricity price point in opposite directions.

item.title: Petrol receipts in Cyprus must show the fuel price and the tax separately
item.description: The House passed a law requiring a receipt that splits the fuel cost from the tax, from 1 February. The same day it extended the cut in fuel excise to the end of March 2027.

item.title: Christodoulides asks companies to cut prices as MPs extend the fuel-tax cut to March 2027 and order a tax breakdown on receipts
item.description: The president called EKO’s heating-fuel discount an act of responsibility and urged other firms to follow. Parliament extended the reduced excise duty to 31 March 2027 and will make stations itemise taxes from 1 February.

item.title: Fitto is due to meet Fidan in Ankara today, while Kokkina stays on the table
item.description: The Commission’s envoy for Cyprus is in the Turkish capital for talks on the Cyprus problem and EU-Turkey relations. Christodoulides told Tylliria communities, Politis reported, that a Kokkina crossing is still under discussion.

item.title: Eden Coast, Geroskipou: what bbf publishes about the Paphos project
item.description: An independent reading of Eden Coast. This is not a developer listing and not a partnership sale. The official page gives a €940,000 start and 16 homes, and it states the sea as both 50 m and 20 metres.

item.title: EAC chairman: grid batteries by next summer, Dhekelia storage in September
item.description: Loizos Loizou told the Cyprus Mail the grid operator’s batteries are expected by next summer, the EAC’s Dhekelia store in September, and a larger Moni store is out to tender.

item.title: Dream Tower, Agios Tychonas: what the developer and agents actually publish
item.description: An independent reading of Dream Tower in Limassol. This is not a sale and not a partnership. The developer page starts at €890,000 and says 150 m to the sea. Agents publish other figures.

item.title: Akel tables a bill to cancel Cyprus camera fines not served within 180 days
item.description: The bill is not law. It would void an out-of-court camera fine that is not served within 180 days, and would add penalty points on the day of the offence.

item.title: Where to stay in Cyprus: Limassol, Paphos, Ayia Napa and Larnaca
item.description: Where to stay in Cyprus: Limassol is the port between Kourion and Amathus, Paphos is UNESCO and PFO airport, Ayia Napa is the Cape Greco resort, Larnaca is Finikoudes and LCA. No hotel rates are printed here.

item.title: Renting a car in Cyprus: prices, insurance and driving rules
item.description: Car hire in Cyprus: drive on the left, 100 km/h maximum and 65 minimum on major highways, 50 in town unless a sign says otherwise. There is no single official daily hire price.

item.title: How to protect your data and accounts when using foreign banks and services
item.description: A foreign bank is not, by itself, less safe than the one you left. The risk is the login, the email that can reset it, and the phone number that receives the code, set up on a network you do not control.

item.title: Mazotos desalination works paused after a third day of protest
item.description: Mazotos desalination protest: works at Petountas are suspended until next week. Police call it a removal from the site; the Greens call it an arrest. The spokesperson was released.

item.title: International health insurance for people who live and work abroad: an honest breakdown
item.description: A policy for a holiday is not a policy for a year abroad. Travel medical cover, a long-stay plan, a European health card and Cyprus’s GeSY answer different questions, and none of the prices are printed here.

item.title: HELLENiQ Energy leaves the door open to a Cyprus offshore gas partnership
item.description: Cyprus gas HELLENiQ Energy: chief executive Andreas Shiamishis said a future role through a partner is still under consideration, but nine Greek blocks are the priority for three to four years.

item.title: EU €3 parcel duty: what Temu and Shein shoppers in Cyprus are complaining about, and how to still save on Black Friday
item.description: EU €3 parcel duty for Temu and Shein: the €150 exemption ended on 1 July 2026, the €3 is per product category, and a €2 handling fee began on 1 November. Cyprus Post adds €3.50.

item.title: eSIM and mobile data in Cyprus for tourists
item.description: eSIM in Cyprus for tourists: the Republic is in the EU, so an EU subscriber is under roam-like-at-home. A separate plan is for a non-EU home SIM. This page does not invent local SIM prices.

item.title: EU wants Cypriot students in Britain to pay home university fees
item.description: Before Friday’s EU–UK summit, Brussels wants European students to pay no more than British students. UK fees are up to £9,790; others can pay up to £35,000 or more.

item.title: Cyprus Mail’s view: housing is the cost of drawing foreign firms
item.description: A Cyprus Mail editorial, not a news report: rising Cyprus housing prices, foreign workers and dearer mortgages, and why the paper calls a large state fix unrealistic.

item.title: Christodoulides and Erhurman to meet in the Nicosia buffer zone on 24 November
item.description: Cyprus talks 24 November: the leaders meet at 15:00. A tripartite with Guterres may come before the end of the month, and an enlarged meeting in early December is still described as possible.

item.title: Best things to do in Cyprus in 2026, city by city
item.description: Things to do in Cyprus in 2026 by city: Nicosia, Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca, Ayia Napa and the Troodos, from the Deputy Ministry of Tourism. Beaches are public, and more than 75 fly a Blue Flag.

item.title: Tax commissioner has the 3,000-page Mafia State report
item.description: Sotiris Markides has spent four months on the anti-corruption file. A bill would let him look back 20 years, not 12. The report’s recommendations are not a conviction.

item.title: Greek direct investment in Cyprus rose to €9.2 billion
item.description: Greek investment in Cyprus reached €9.2 billion by June 2026, from €5.6 billion in 2024, Invest Cyprus said. Cypriot investment in Greece is about €2.7 billion.

item.title: Digital Citizen now stores foreign residents’ residence documents
item.description: EU and third-country nationals in Cyprus can add a residence document to Digital Citizen, and children’s Cypriot ID cards can be added too. Originals are still needed to travel.

item.title: Cyprus to join the Schengen zone on 1 July 2027, Mitsotakis says
item.description: Cyprus Schengen 2027: Mitsotakis says the island joins on 1 July, the day Greece takes the EU Council presidency. The Green Line question is still open.

item.title: Cyprus inflation rose to 5.4% in October 2026, above the eurozone
item.description: Cyprus inflation October 2026: the harmonised rate hit 5.4%, up from 5.2% in September and from 0.2% a year earlier. The eurozone average was 4%.

item.title: Christodoulides and Mitsotakis open the fourth Cyprus–Greece summit in Nicosia
item.description: Artificial intelligence, civil protection and the passage from the Cypriot to the Greek EU presidency lead Wednesday's agenda. The spokesman put 24 ministers and deputy ministers in the two delegations.

item.title: Cyprus construction material prices rose 4.09% in October 2026
item.description: Construction materials Cyprus October 2026: the index hit 123.90, base 2021, up 0.39% on the month and 4.09% on the year. Electrical fixtures rose 9.54%, the steepest line in the release.

item.title: Cabinet weighs a single Cyprus water tariff, with €10 a cubic metre above 81
item.description: The interior ministry wants one scale for the whole island, caps on sewerage and stormwater fees, and a lower band for vulnerable households. The cabinet had not voted on Tuesday morning, and parliament would still have to approve the texts.

item.title: Letymbiotis: Cyprus will consent to Turkey customs talks if Cyprus talks resume
item.description: The condition is substantive negotiations from where they stopped at Crans-Montana in 2017. The spokesman tied that to Ankara's wish to upgrade the customs union with the EU.

item.title: Tourist arrivals are down 5.6 per cent over ten months, and October lost 29,000
item.description: The statistical service counted 3.91 million arrivals from January to October, almost 233,000 fewer than a year earlier. October wiped out September's gain.

item.title: Moving to Cyprus: the first months, the residence routes, and the tax
item.description: There is no statute called the first 90 days. The clocks are the ones departments publish: four months for MEU1, a pink slip before the visa expires, a driving-licence exchange after 185 days. A residence card does not make a person tax resident.

item.title: Provident funds would start voluntary, and could become compulsory in three to four years
item.description: Politis and Phileleftheros set out Labour Minister Marinos Mousiouttas’s proposal: bring in 50 to 60 per cent of workers who have no fund now. If that fails, a law would make membership compulsory. The opening contribution is 1.5 per cent each from worker and employer.

item.title: Bills for the 2028 vote would lift the spending cap to €1.7 million and the campaign to 12 months
item.description: On Thursday the interior committee starts on two bills from AKEL and Direct Democracy. Politis says the changes have to be voted by February if they are to apply to the presidential election.

item.title: 53 years after the Polytechnic uprising, Nicosia students march to the US embassy
item.description: In Athens the Polytechnic courtyards are open from 9am to 1pm, the buildings stay shut, and more than 5,000 police are posted. The Pancyprian pupil committee gathers at 10:30 at Pasydy and walks to the American embassy.

item.title: No Cyprus internet cut is scheduled for 17 November; the global blackout claim is false
item.description: Viral warnings of a power, internet and banking blackout do not match any Cypriot provider notice. The dated event is a short US radio and television alert test.

item.title: Nicosia condemns Ustel's "new Varosha" and takes it to the United Nations
item.description: On Monday he said the plan was ready and would change occupied Famagusta. On Tuesday Letymbiotis said the fenced city is governed by resolutions 550 and 789, and unilateral steps are not allowed.

item.title: New housing loans in September: Cyprus 3.26%, Germany 4.09%
item.description: The ECB average on new euro loans for house purchase in September 2026 was 3.26% in Cyprus, 4.09% in Germany, 3.24% in Greece and 2.99% in Spain. It is not a bank’s offer. The Central Bank of Cyprus caps loan-to-value at 80% for a primary residence and 70% for other property.

item.title: Paris says it fully supports the Great Sea Interconnector
item.description: A French foreign ministry spokesman on Monday called the cable strategically important and necessary to link Cyprus to the EU energy network. The survey ship Abeille Marengo has left Heraklion. A professor quoted by Alithia sees the note to Ankara as a dangerous precedent.

item.title: Erhurman puts the odds of a Guterres trilateral at "51 to 49"
item.description: On Tuesday he said he was selling neither false hope nor despair, and that he expected "something new" to emerge. A trilateral, he said, means negotiating with the Turkish Cypriots, not with Turkey.

item.title: Senekis: more than €200 million for water, and four new permanent desalination plants
item.description: The agriculture minister called it the costliest bet on water security since the Kouris Dam and the Southern Conveyor. The aim is to meet drinking-water needs from desalination and leave the reservoirs to farmers.

item.title: A new Cyprus resident’s checklist: tax code, yellow slip, GESY and the return
item.description: It is not one card. A 2026 handbook sets out the tax code, the yellow slip and the pink slip, GESY, the income-tax return, social insurance, a bank account and the driving-licence exchange, with the fee or deadline each department prints.

item.title: Commission: Cyprus growth slows to 3 per cent in 2027, inflation to 2.9
item.description: Tuesday's autumn forecast still puts the island well above the eurozone. Higher energy prices, the Commission says, will weigh on spending for a while.

item.title: Christodoulides wants a meeting with Erhurman before the next UN trilateral
item.description: On Monday the president said the negotiators would discuss such a meeting on Tuesday. The UN has given no date yet. He also welcomed the reply on friendly matches and said work has started on the Louroujina–Lympia and Kambos–Karavostasi crossings.

item.title: Hundreds of graves at Saints Constantine and Helen were sold more than once, a church official estimates
item.description: Andreas Karayiorgis, secretary of the cemetery church committee, tells Phileleftheros of 700 to 750 repeat sales. Archbishop Georgios says he will act if the complaints hold. Karayiorgis himself calls one 2003 receipt a forgery.

item.title: Man found with knife wounds near Kykkos Monastery is in intensive care after surgery
item.description: An ambulance crew found him on Monday morning on a rural road. Reports differ on whether police have identified him.

item.title: Cyprus unveils Kyrenia 3, its first locally built satellite
item.description: A space-weather centre also began operating in Nicosia. No launch date has been set for the three satellites shown on Monday.

item.title: Letymbiotis: Cyprus is "very close" on the Mia Milia and Athienou–Pyroi crossings
item.description: Nicosia is waiting for the UN to date the next trilateral, and says the president has not accepted Erhürman's proposal. The €25 million for the electricity link has not been paid.

item.title: POED and OELMEK skip the education minister's meeting on teacher appointments
item.description: The dispute is over permanent posts for about 4,000 teachers without the exam required by the 2015 law. OLTEK did attend.

item.title: Cypriot students in Greece marched on Turkish missions on the anniversary of the "TRNC"
item.description: On Sunday, the 43rd anniversary of the unilateral declaration, there were marches in Athens, Komotini and Thessaloniki. In Thessaloniki police kept the columns back from the consulate.

item.title: Wanted suspect in alleged Limassol murder plot arrested at Dubai airport, reports say
item.description: The case concerns an alleged €800,000 plot to kill Giorgos Xiourouppas; Cypriot authorities are still waiting for official confirmation from the UAE, the same reports say.

item.title: Cyprus is producing copper again: Hellenic Cuprum turns out 99.999% pure cathodes
item.description: SXEW Hellenic Cuprum is operating at the Skouriotissa and Apliki mines, exporting all of its output, and since June 2026 has covered a substantial share of its power use with its own solar plant.

item.title: 44-year-old woman found dead in Nicosia as police search for a third person; flat reportedly used as a massage parlour
item.description: Police are treating the case as suspected premeditated murder and attempted murder after a second woman was found injured at a nearby junction.

item.title: Admie: Greece–Cyprus electricity link is planned for completion by the end of 2031
item.description: The Greek operator’s 10-year development plan sets the date, a budget of about €1.94 billion, and an estimate that wholesale prices in Cyprus could fall by around 19%.

item.title: 2025 income tax returns can still be filed without penalties until 30 November
item.description: The formal deadline was 31 October, but the Tax Department has given until the end of the month to file form T.F.1 and pay — without interest or monetary charges.

item.title: This weekend, 14–15 November: festivals, the Larnaca marathon and Cyprus v Montenegro
item.description: Four cities host a wellbeing festival, a book fair, family concerts and the 9th Radisson Hotels Larnaka Marathon.

item.title: Damianos: Cyprus wants fintech jobs, not only company registrations
item.description: At the Cyprus Fintech Summit the commerce minister said the test is whether firms build teams on the island. Preliminary research puts the sector near 200 companies.

item.title: Labour ministry opens a campaign on professional drivers’ hours
item.description: The drive runs until 22 November, after more than 1,300 inspections in three years found breaches of driving and rest rules.

item.title: Auditor general: planning law still not enforced at a Nicosia venue
item.description: A music and dance reception venue has operated since October 2023 without meeting permit conditions set by the Cabinet in 2022.

item.title: Helicopters and drones search Paphos forest for missing mushroom picker
item.description: A 60-year-old Turkish Cypriot vanished in the Cedar Valley area on Thursday; searches continued through the night and into Friday.

item.title: More than a third of people with diabetes in Cyprus do not know they have it
item.description: Ahead of World Diabetes Day on 14 November, endocrinologists urge early checks; free screenings are planned across the island.

item.title: Crossing-camera fine cost the state €1.2m and has produced 2,500 bookings
item.description: Phileleftheros reports that the €85 penalty for stopping on camera-monitored crossings required a costly system upgrade and has caught few drivers.

item.title: Over €51.5 million in assets frozen in Cyprus since 2023, half tied to golden passports
item.description: Police told the House audit committee that asset freezes have risen sharply, while an Audit Office report flagged gaps in banking supervision.

item.title: Cape Greco: planning council meets on legalising an unauthorised monastery in a Natura 2000 area
item.description: After an October vote in favour caused uproar, the Council for the Study of Deviations is finalising its opinion for the Cabinet on Friday.

item.title: Pension bill is held at the Legal Service over benefits for Europeans who worked in Cyprus
item.description: The 1 January 2027 target still stands, but the minister told parliament on Monday that covering non-residents would mean about €100 million the funds cannot bear.

item.title: Microsoft says the global outage is over and traces it to a July software defect
item.description: The company said on Saturday that service was restored. A preliminary report links the failure to a July change in the network gateways that surfaced on 12 November.

item.title: EU leaders hold first-ever summit on artificial intelligence in Dublin
item.description: Cyprus is represented by President Christodoulides at an informal gathering that comes days after Nicosia adopted its own national AI strategy.

item.title: Cyprus wants to make video games, not just host game companies
item.description: A deputy minister outlined plans at the Cyprus Games Summit in Limassol, citing an industry report that puts annual game revenue at around €3.2 billion.

item.title: EU envoy Fitto to carry the Cyprus question to Ankara on 20 November
item.description: President Christodoulides and the EU's special representative on the Cyprus problem spoke by phone on Thursday to prepare the envoy's talks with Turkey's foreign minister.

item.title: 330 families told to leave caravan site at Governor's Beach
item.description: MPs heard that notices were posted at the Limassol site after the operator's contract expired; about 102 of the families live there permanently.

item.title: Nicosia Christmas market returns to Eleftheria Square for a second year
item.description: From 28 November to 27 December, more than 45 local handmade makers will fill the square, with free entry.

item.title: Aris Kiayias wins Cyprus's first Youth Olympic fencing medal
item.description: The foil bronze in Dakar is Cyprus's fourth medal at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, sealed by three straight points in a 15–14 finish.

item.title: Selling property in Cyprus: fines of up to €100,000 for missed obligations
item.description: Sellers must attach a fresh land-registry search certificate to the sale contract, and lenders must release mortgages on time — or face administrative penalties.

item.title: Finished, but not deliverable: new homes in Paphos wait for electricity
item.description: A legal commentary describes buyers who have paid for completed homes that cannot be connected to the grid, with the waiting time tied to an authority that is not party to their contracts.
